passage: On the drawing-room floor, Madhav stared at one gap in his jigsaw. He picked up a piece and pushed it in. No. Another. No. A third, turned round twice. No. His sister Bhavna, sipping juice on the sofa, watched him. He did not once look at the picture on the box lid. Piece after piece went to the same gap until a green one with two knobs clicked in. "It fits!" said Madhav, and reached into the pile to look for the next gap.

qa.q: How did Madhav find the piece that fitted?
qa.a: Madhav tried piece after piece at the same gap until a green one with two knobs clicked in.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling when the green piece clicked in?
qa.a: Madhav felt pleased and excited, and he shouted, "It fits!" He was ready straight away for the next gap.

qa.q: What other approach could speed up the puzzle, and why?
qa.a: Madhav could look at the picture on the box lid and match colours, or sort the flat-sided pieces first. Fewer wrong tries would be needed.

qa.q: How does Madhav's way of solving the puzzle look to Bhavna?
qa.a: Bhavna sees her brother try one piece after another without looking at the picture. It may look slow, but he does not give up.

grounding: A child tries one piece after another at the same gap until one fits, without thinking about the picture.

passage:
"This one?" Rukmini pressed a piece into the gap. It didn't fit.
"Try the next," said Harish, her brother.
"This one?" No.
"Look at the picture on it," Harish said.
"I don't need to." She tried another, and another, turning each one. "This one?" Click. "Yes!"
Harish laughed. "It took you nine tries."
"But I got it."

qa.q: How many tries did it take Rukmini?
What was Rukmini feeling when she said "But I got it"?
qa.a: She was proud and pleased, even though it took many tries.

qa.q: What else could Rukmini try to be faster?
qa.a: Look at the picture on each piece, as Harish said, to find matching colours.

qa.q: How does her trying look to Harish?
qa.a: Harish finds it funny and a bit slow, and wants her to use the picture.

grounding: A child tries piece after piece at the same jigsaw gap until one fits, without using the picture.

passage:
Note for Sahil's parents
Today Sahil did the farm jigsaw. For the gap near the cow, he tried piece after piece, turning each, until one clicked, about ten tries. He never looked at the colours. His friend Akash said, "That one's brown, like the cow." Sahil tried the brown piece next. I pointed at the pictures later to show him.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling as he kept trying?
qa.a: He seemed determined and patient, not frustrated.

qa.q: What did the note-writer do, and why might it help?
qa.a: They pointed at the pictures later, to show him how colours can guide where pieces go.

qa.q: How does Sahil's method look to Akash?
qa.a: Akash sees a quicker way using the colours and wants to help.

grounding: A teacher's note describes a child who tries piece after piece at the same gap without looking at the picture.
